issues.summary: The documented data undo is not runnable as written. TODO.md:67-69 tells the 3am operator to "run restoreWeekFromHealBackup_('YYYY-MM-DD') from the editor", but that function (Code.gs:1935) takes a REQUIRED argument the editor's Run button cannot supply, and is underscore-suffixed (Apps Script treats a trailing underscore as private — excluded from the Run function picker and from google.script.run). No zero-arg wrapper exists: grep shows the only non-test references are the definition, its own Logger line, and the TODO.md sentence. Every other operator-facing repair entry point in this project is a no-underscore, zero-arg wrapper (runSummaryDriftRepair, runSummaryOrphanSweep, cleanupDuplicateSummaryRows, previewSummaryHeal, auditSummaryDrift). Failure is at least fail-closed — invoked with no arg, week is undefined, no backup row matches, and it returns {refused:'no-snapshot'} without touching live rows — but the operator must author and save a wrapper mid-incident on the ONLY path that undoes a bad heal (TODO.md:70-72 states a code rollback cannot). Step 7's FIX3 test6a (test_code.js:9281) was written for exactly this discoverability concern but only asserts the identifier string appears in TODO.md, so it passes while the function remains uncallable. Add a wrapper such as restoreSummaryWeek(week) and name that in the runbook.

restoreWeekFromHealBackup_ (Code.gs:1935) reads the live Summary range, then deletes that week's rows and appends the snapshot, with no withScriptLock_ — unlike weeklySummarize (Code.gs:2273) and every scheduled/ingest entry point. This matches sibling manual tools (cleanupDuplicateSummaryRows, runSummaryOrphanSweep are also unlocked), so it is existing convention rather than drift introduced here, and the delete-from-the-end-backwards loop is index-safe against appendRow. But this tool is explicitly documented for 3am incident use, when the 04:00 weeklySummarize trigger may fire: a concurrent heal's upsert can interleave with the restore's delete+append and be silently lost. Wrapping the restore in withScriptLock_ is cheap given it already returns a {refused:...} shape for the lock-timeout case.

healEarliestBackupRows_ (Code.gs:1909) hardcodes row[8] as run_id, while its only caller restoreWeekFromHealBackup_ slices restored rows with SUMMARY_HEADERS.length (Code.gs:1963). Both are correct today (SUMMARY_HEADERS has 8 entries, SUMMARY_HEAL_BACKUP_HEADERS = SUMMARY_HEADERS.concat(['run_id'])), but the two encodings of the same fact disagree the moment a column is added: run_id would move while row[8] keeps reading a data column, so snapshot tie-breaking would silently mix two snapshots' rows and the restore would write a blended week. This is the same latent class as the project's documented 'header consts do not migrate live tabs' gotcha. Use SUMMARY_HEADERS.length (or a named SUMMARY_BACKUP_RUNID_COL) in both places.

The raiseCalendarAlert_ extraction (staleness.gs:~296) moved the getEventsForDay read inside the per-alert primitive. stalenessRaiseAlerts_ previously did ONE calendar read for the whole batch and tested each title against that map; it now calls raiseCalendarAlert_ once per stale source, so the day's events are re-read once per alert. Same for healRaiseAlert_, which fires per healed week (up to SUMMARY_HEAL_WEEKS=4 per run) and per SPLIT/duplicate refusal. Behaviour is unchanged and correctness is unaffected — this is only Calendar read-quota and latency on a path that runs on a schedule. If the source list grows, hoist the day-read back to the caller or memoize it per invocation.
